To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
all 3 IR indexes were significantly associated with cardiometabolic parameters, but there was no significant difference in their ability in predicting cardiometabolic conditions.

all 3 indexes significantly correlate with indicators of cardiometabolic profile, but only the differences in correlation with waist and mean carotid intima media thickness were statistically significant.
the HOMA AD is the best index of IR for predicting metabolic syndrome in obese individuals, but all 3 indexes are not superior in predicting cardiometabolic abnormalities in obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the surrogate markers of IR and the cardiometabolic profiles in a population of obese subjects.
the evaluation of different IR indexes, their correlation with cardiometabolic profile parameters, as well as the prediction of cardiometabolic risk factors.
the evaluation of the surrogate markers of IR and the cardiometabolic risk in obese individuals without previous diagnosis of diabetes mellitus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3 indexes are not superior compared to the other two.
all 3 indices are useful for the evaluation of IR in obese patients, but the HOMA AD seems to have better performances in predicting the presence of metabolic syndrome.
all 3 indexes are useful tools to identify the obese individuals at high risk for cardiometabolic complications, but the choice of the most appropriate index is not possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all 3 indexes are useful in predicting cardiometabolic risk in obese individuals.
the three indexes are not superior compared to the HOMA-IR, in the identification obese individuals with a cardiometabolic risk profile.

HOMA AD is a good index to identify obese patients with metabolic syndrome, MI is the best to identify obese patients at risk of NAFLD and HOMA IR is the best to detect obese patients with increased CAIMT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HOMA IR index can be used to assess IR in obesity, and it may have a predictive value in the identification of patients at higher cardiovascular risk.
all 3 IR indexes are useful in the evaluation of obese subjects with a cardiometabolic risk.
the HOMA AD index, as well as MI, is a good surrogate for the assessment of IR in obese individuals, without previous history of type 2 diabetes.
